clue.text: Any other cruciverbalists detest vacuous Listeners to fill in?

indicators.note: the cruciverbalists' pronoun is a frame that the following material is put inside to fill

parts.note: the pronoun crossword solvers use of themselves as a community
a plain synonym for loathe

indicators.note: something vacuous is empty inside, so the word Listeners loses everything except its two ends

parts.note: just the outside letters of the word

explanation.surface: A sly dig suggesting crossword solvers loathe the empty Listener grids they must fill in.
explanation.walkthrough: The Listener is a famously hard puzzle series in The Times, which makes 'Listeners' look like the subject; it only supplies its two outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase asks whether anything further or additional remains, the same idea as another one besides those already mentioned.

clue.text: See 22
Change steps used by people in the country to stop epidemic

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so the rural steps go inside the coins like a stopper

parts.note: loose change counted in British coins

parts.words: steps used by people in the country
parts.note: a set of steps letting walkers climb over a farm fence

explanation.surface: Some rule change about walkers' steps in the countryside is supposed to halt an outbreak.
explanation.walkthrough: A stile is a set of steps over a field wall or fence, common on British footpaths; one went in the countryside closure rules of foot-and-mouth outbreaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A pestilence is a deadly infectious disease sweeping through a population, which is what an epidemic describes.

clue.text: Goddess sometimes symbolised as owl, subsequently as shepherd

indicators.note: a shepherd keeps a flock gathered between them, so the pair of letters herds the word for subsequently between them

parts.note: read as the plural of the letter A: two As
a plain synonym for afterwards

explanation.surface: A note on how a Greek goddess has been depicted in art, first as a bird and later as a herdsman.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'as' looks like a comparison word, but it is the plural of the letter A, and 'shepherd' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Athena, Greek deity of wisdom, is traditionally accompanied or represented by the little owl, so her image is often that bird.

clue.text: Comedy series go, and I should have mentioned how

parts.note: to go is an informal way of saying to urinate
a postscript adds what the writer forgot to say earlier
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone recommending a sitcom, then adding they forgot to explain how to watch it.
explanation.walkthrough: PEEP SHOW is a British TV sitcom (2003 to 2015) starring Mitchell and Webb.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of a long-running Channel 4 sitcom, so it is an example of a television comedy programme.

clue.text: Crow when this bundle of hay produces crop

indicators.note: the instruction is to read the solution itself as a rule for swapping one letter of the bird for another

parts.note: the last letter of the bird's name, the one to be replaced
the letter that turns the bird into a harvest

explanation.surface: A farming riddle in which a black bird and a handful of hay somehow yield a harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as W IS P: when W is P, crow becomes crop. The solution itself is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A wisp is a small twist or handful of straw or hay, a light tuft of loose stalks.

clue.text: Farewell to Naruhito, perhaps working at intervals abroad

parts.note: as in 'say, ten people', meaning for example
a machine that is on is working

indicators.note: at intervals means taking letters spaced evenly through the following word, every other one

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of the word

explanation.surface: Saying goodbye to Japan's emperor, perhaps while posted overseas from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: Naruhito is the present Emperor of Japan, which points to a Japanese word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sayonara is the Japanese word for goodbye, so it is the parting greeting one would use with a Japanese emperor.

clue.text: They go down south with several families coming north

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming north means moving higher up the column, so the families word is placed in front of the several word

parts.note: compass abbreviation
relatives collectively
a literary word meaning sundry or various

explanation.surface: Pictures a big migration: people heading south while several family groups travel north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' is an old-fashioned word for several, as in 'divers reasons'. 'They go down south' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'down'.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin-divers swim underwater without diving suits, so they descend beneath the surface of the sea.

clue.text: Large bear has cut in two

indicators.note: the verb for bear holds or has the size letter inside it

parts.note: as in giving birth: to bear a child is to have one
clothing-size abbreviation

explanation.surface: A big bear has been sliced down the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To halve something is to divide it into two equal parts, which is what this phrase describes as an action.

clue.text: Hamlet on vacation there? It can make plays

definitions.text: Hamlet on vacation there? It can make plays

indicators.note: the letters play about, moving freely into a new order
vacated means emptied out, so the Danish prince's name keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: the play title with its middle removed
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pictures a summer-holiday staging of Shakespeare at a seaside venue that puts on plays.
explanation.walkthrough: The Minack Theatre is an open-air theatre cut into the cliffs near Land's End in Cornwall; the whole clue describes it and also supplies the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A clifftop amphitheatre in a holiday county is just the kind of place a visitor might watch the Danish tragedy while on holiday.

clue.text: See 10
Snack food element of dad jokes?

parts.note: an informal name for one's father
corny humour, stale and obvious jokes

explanation.surface: Asks whether groan-worthy fathers' jokes have a certain ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 3,4 the answer reads as 'pop corn', and corny jokes are exactly what dad jokes are.
explanation.definitionFit: Popcorn is a popular snack made from heated maize kernels that burst open, eaten at cinemas.

clue.text: Rack sadistic — change of heart required

indicators.note: the heart is the central letter, which must be changed for another

parts.note: enjoying inflicting pain; its middle vowel is the one swapped

explanation.surface: Torture on the rack is sadistic, and the torturer needs to repent.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the U in the middle of the word for E. 'Rack' looks like a torture device but is a frame for holding things.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a frame or stand holding bobbins in spinning, or a fisherman's basket, so a kind of rack.

clue.text: Spooner's big cats rate juice producer

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of word pairs, so the next two words trade their first sounds

parts.note: a pride is a group of lions; it hands over its PR sound and takes an S sound, picking up the following A
to rate something is to assess it; it hands its S sound forward and takes PR

explanation.surface: Spooner is grading some large felines.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'pride assess' with the opening sounds swapped and you get 'side a press', which sounds just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cider press squeezes crushed apples so that their liquid runs out, the first stage of making the drink.

clue.text: Jewish pasty John's initially bitten into?

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word bites its way inside the word for pale

parts.note: pale-faced, as the adjective pasty means
john and kazi are both slang for a lavatory

explanation.surface: Asks whether a pale Jewish pastry has had a bite taken out of it.
explanation.walkthrough: John is American slang for a toilet; kazi (or khazi) is British slang for the same. Its K moves into the pale word and the rest follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashkenazi describes Jews of central and eastern European descent, one of the main Jewish ethnic groups.

clue.text: Items chef uses maybe where we are restaurant customers

parts.note: for example, abbreviated
the Telegraph speaks from Great Britain
diners are the people who eat there

explanation.surface: Kitchen gear a cook might use, perhaps where we sit as diners.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg beaters are whisks used in the kitchen to whip eggs, standard tools for a cook.

clue.text: Perform self-destructive actions like crazy drinking no more, put in the ground

indicators.note: the verb for like takes the following words in, as a drinker takes in a drink

parts.note: dated slang, as in 'I dig jazz'
departed or finished
as seeds are
to rave is to talk wildly, as if crazy; a rave is also a craze

explanation.surface: A drunk warned that boozing like mad will see them buried before long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put in the ground' looks like burial and chimes with the definition, but it means sowing seed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to bring about one's own downfall through one's own behaviour, which is self-destruction.

clue.text: Gets assistance denied

parts.note: obtains
help

explanation.surface: Someone receives help that had been refused.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to contradict or deny, so its past tense means contradicted or disputed.

clue.text: Section of newspaper attacks rising stable staff

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word for attacks is read from the bottom up

parts.note: informal: to lam someone is to thrash them
young racing-stable workers are called lads

explanation.surface: A news report on stable hands growing violent.
explanation.walkthrough: Lads is the racing term for grooms at a racehorse stable, of either sex. Small ads are the classified advertisements.
explanation.definitionFit: The classified pages, where private individuals place brief notices for things to buy or sell, form part of a paper.

clue.text: First-time parents did cause a commotion

definitions.meaning: Adam and Eve, the first parents in Genesis, brought up their firstborn son
the idiom for making an angry fuss

explanation.walkthrough: 'First-time parents' sounds like any new mum and dad; it means the very first parents of all, in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to create uproar or trouble, from Cain's violent reputation in Genesis.

clue.text: Century: ten I need to have brought this up

definitions.text: Century: ten I need to have brought this up

indicators.note: in a down entry, bringing something up means reading the letters bottom to top
the opening words are said to have, or contain, the answer within their run of letters

parts.note: the letter run straddling the end of the first word, the next two words and the start of the fourth

explanation.surface: A batsman on ninety reckons ten more runs will bring up a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue is the sum: ten more brings this number up to a hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: One hundred minus ten leaves ninety, the score a batsman needs ten more on to reach a century.

clue.text: End of double lines of people repeatedly missing same play

indicators.note: the same letter as the one just taken is dropped, and more than once
only the final letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: its final letter
people standing in line

explanation.surface: A theatre scene: at the end of a double bill, the queues go missing the same play.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Es come out of the queues word, the same letter just taken from the end of double.
explanation.definitionFit: Equus is a 1973 stage drama by Peter Shaffer about a boy who blinds horses, so it is a play.

clue.text: United staff, head claimed the day before, part of the reserves?

parts.note: standard abbreviation, as in football club names

indicators.note: the staff claims, or takes hold of, the head word inside itself

parts.note: a long stick
a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness
as in Christmas Eve

explanation.surface: A football club's staff sees the boss pick his team the day before, with some players in the reserves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' and 'reserves' suggest a football club; a ness is a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept up one's sleeve is held back secretly for later use, so it is among a person's reserves.

clue.text: Fluster free?

indicators.note: set free, the letters of the preceding word are released to rearrange

parts.note: taken as written, all seven letters

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: freed from fluster is calm, and freeing the word's letters gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Restful means calm and soothing, the state of being without agitation or nervous bother.

clue.text: Military instrument — fine, albeit electronic

parts.note: pencil-grade abbreviation
as in 'a good, if long, film'
as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A military band player approves of an instrument even though it is an electric one.
explanation.definitionFit: The fife is a small high flute played with drums in marching bands, especially in armies.

clue.text: Like CO, maybe, it is recommended more than usual

definitions.meaning: carbon monoxide is a poisonous gas that should never be inhaled
the idiom for something worth taking seriously

explanation.walkthrough: CO looks like a commanding officer; it is the chemical formula for carbon monoxide.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something worth having and not to be dismissed, so it deserves more than ordinary endorsement.

clue.text: See 1
See 25
Run them off limits when they won't take off

parts.note: cricket scoring abbreviation

indicators.note: with its limits off, the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: the inner letters only
as in 'as I arrived'

explanation.surface: An order to chase some creatures out of a forbidden area while they stay grounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' sounds like removing something, but it means leaving the ground in flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheas are large flightless South American birds, so they never become airborne.
